title: Usher — 5 Cost & Compliance
description: LLM spend, embedding compute, bulk-dataset freshness, disk headroom, and the TMDb cache-age panel that is a licence term rather than a metric.

panels.title: TMDb cache age against the 6-month ceiling
panels.description:
🔴 **The one panel here whose failure is a licence breach, and the reason it is not trimmed.** Every other panel on this dashboard is a blind spot when it breaks; this one is a term of TMDb's licence. `tests/unit/test_no_third_party_data.py` enforces the redistribution half of that licence mechanically; **nothing enforces the retention half**, and this panel plus its threshold is the whole of it.

Reads `raw_payloads.fetched_at` — when the payload was cached — and deliberately **not** `titles.enriched_at`, which records when Usher enriched a title and does not move when a cached payload is re-read. Spelled `interval '6 months'` and never `'180 days'`: the two are never equal and 180 days matches *more* rows, so it over-reports a breach that has not happened.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT min(raw_payloads.fetched_at) AS oldest_fetched_at,
       now() - interval '6 months' AS ceiling
FROM raw_payloads
WHERE raw_payloads.provider = 'tmdb';

panels.title: TMDb entries past the ceiling
panels.description:
The breach count itself. **`<`, never `<=`** — TMDb's term is *no more than 6 months*, so a payload cached exactly six months ago is still in term.

Measured 2026-09-07 on the live catalog: **0 past the ceiling** over 133,631 cached payloads, oldest 2026-08-11. That was the first time anyone had looked.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS past_ceiling
FROM raw_payloads
WHERE raw_payloads.provider = 'tmdb'
  AND raw_payloads.fetched_at < now() - interval '6 months';

panels.title: Past-ceiling share of the cache
panels.description:
The count as a share of the cache, and the denominator beside it. `NULLIF` guards the empty cache, where the honest answer is NULL rather than a division by zero.

⚠️ **Three statements and not one.** `count(*)` reads every row, so folding the three together costs the other two their index: measured, separately 0.48 / 4.46 ms with `ix_raw_payloads_fetched_at`, combined one `Parallel Seq Scan` with the index unused.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS cached,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE raw_payloads.fetched_at < now() - interval '6 months')::numeric
         / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS past_ceiling_share
FROM raw_payloads
WHERE raw_payloads.provider = 'tmdb';

panels.title: LLM spend by model and purpose
panels.description:
⚠️ **A dashboard reading $0.00 is not evidence of a free deployment.** `cost_usd` defaults to `0`, which is the honest value against a local model and the **wrong** value for a hosted model an operator forgot to price. The mitigation is that `tokens_in` and `tokens_out` are exact, so spend is recomputable after the fact — which is why this panel plots the tokens beside the money rather than the money alone.

Verified live 2026-08-07: `0.00000000` against a local model, and `0.01658700` with prices 3/15 per Mtok configured — exactly `Decimal((4359×3 + 234×15) / 1e6)`, the column `numeric` and `SUM()` agreeing to 8 decimal places.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT llm_calls.model, llm_calls.purpose,
       sum(llm_calls.cost_usd)   AS cost_usd,
       sum(llm_calls.tokens_in)  AS tokens_in,
       sum(llm_calls.tokens_out) AS tokens_out,
       count(*) AS calls
FROM llm_calls
GROUP BY llm_calls.model, llm_calls.purpose
ORDER BY cost_usd DESC;

panels.title: Cost per curated row
panels.description:
`llm_calls ⋈ curated_rows USING (generation_id)` **and nothing else** — one join wide.

⚠️ **Which population this reads depends on a setting.** `ix_llm_calls_generation_id` is partial (`WHERE generation_id IS NOT NULL`) because query expansion writes `NULL` there. On the shipped default — `USHER_QUERY_EXPANSION_ENABLED=false` even where the LLM is on — the table is 100% `curation` and the partial index degenerates to a full one. The panel is correct under both, but the same panel over an expansion-enabled deployment is reading a minority of rows.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT curated_rows.generation_id,
       count(DISTINCT curated_rows.id) AS rows_generated,
       sum(llm_calls.cost_usd) AS cost_usd,
       sum(llm_calls.cost_usd) / NULLIF(count(DISTINCT curated_rows.id), 0) AS cost_per_row
FROM llm_calls
JOIN curated_rows USING (generation_id)
GROUP BY curated_rows.generation_id
ORDER BY curated_rows.generation_id DESC
LIMIT 50;

panels.title: Embedding compute time
panels.description:
The one Prometheus panel on this dashboard. `usher.embedding.duration` carries no labels.

⚠️ **Plotted as a mean (`rate(_sum)/rate(_count)`) and not a quantile**, for issue #86's reason: this instrument declares no `explicit_bucket_boundaries_advisory` and `configure_metrics` installs no `View`, so it takes the SDK's default second-scale boundaries. A `histogram_quantile` over those answers a flat plausible number rather than failing — measured at 2.5000 s against a true 35.20 ms.

panels.title: Bulk dataset freshness
panels.description: One row per bulk dataset, from `import_runs`. `heartbeat_at` is what distinguishes a run that is still working from one that died — `finished_at` alone cannot.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT import_runs.dataset, import_runs.status,
       import_runs.started_at, import_runs.heartbeat_at, import_runs.finished_at,
       now() - coalesce(import_runs.finished_at, import_runs.heartbeat_at,
                        import_runs.started_at) AS age
FROM import_runs
ORDER BY coalesce(import_runs.finished_at, import_runs.heartbeat_at,
                  import_runs.started_at) DESC
LIMIT 20;

panels.title: Table size, and headroom against measured free disk
panels.description:
🔴 **Plotted against *measured* free disk, never against PRD 08's resource table.** That table carries its own red warning — *"sizing estimates for an operator provisioning a disk. Nothing in this project reads them, no host enforces them and no policy is derived from them"* — and M9's Track 2 treated one row as a budget, derived a 2.0 GB ceiling from it, and **withdrew a design** measured at 2.702 GB against a number with no forcing function. A number nothing enforces is not a threshold.

This is the panel D13's disk-projection alert is drawn from, and **the window is the same in both: a 7-day least-squares fit extrapolated 14 days** (`predict_linear(system_filesystem_usage_bytes{state="free"}[7d], 14 * 86400) < 0`). Not a shorter one: this deployment's growth is dominated by events days apart — a bootstrap, a crawl, a `similar --rebuild` — and an hour extrapolated to a fortnight would page on every `VACUUM`.

⚠️ **The free-disk denominator is not in this table and cannot be.** This panel is the numerator; the Postgres datasource has no portable way to read a filesystem's free space, so the denominator is `system_filesystem_usage_bytes{state="free"}` — produced by the OTel collector's `hostmetrics` receiver, which the shared stack does not run today, which is why D13's rule ships with an `absent()` companion. Measured 2026-09-11: `pg_database_size('usher_catalog')` **8,384,394,931 B (7,996 MB)** at 1,276,268 titles with 133,576 enriched, against **677,427,249,152 B free** on `/`.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT pg_class.relname AS table_name,
       pg_total_relation_size(pg_class.oid) AS total_bytes,
       pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(pg_class.oid)) AS total_pretty
FROM pg_class
JOIN pg_namespace ON pg_namespace.oid = pg_class.relnamespace
WHERE pg_namespace.nspname = 'public' AND pg_class.relkind = 'r'
ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(pg_class.oid) DESC
LIMIT 25;
